Create observation data from trees

Source: R/createInputs.R
makeObsData.Rd

Derives stand metrics by site/patch/species/year from tree measurements, filters sites, harmonizes years, optionally aggregates by site.

Usage

makeObsData(
  tree_dt,
  plotsize,
  aggregate_by_site = TRUE,
  minNyears = 2,
  fix_period_length = NULL,
  dbh_growth_thresh = c(-10, 50),
  Npatches = NULL,
  Nspecies = NULL,
  NspeciesQuantile = NULL,
  rates = c("annual", "interval")
)

Arguments

tree_dt

data.table of tree records with siteName, patchName, year, treeName, species_name, dbh, status (one of "alive", "new", "dead") and living. Mortality is derived from status; a mort column, if present, is ignored.

plotsize

numeric plot area used to scale recruitment.

aggregate_by_site

logical. Aggregate patches to site level. Default TRUE.

minNyears

integer or NULL. Keep sites with at least this many years and equal counts across patches. Default 2.

fix_period_length

integer or NULL. If set, drop sites whose inventory interval differs. Default NULL.

dbh_growth_thresh

length-2 numeric or NULL. Drop sites where any tree dbh change falls outside this range. Default c(-10, 50).

Npatches

integer or NULL. If set, keep only sites with exactly this many patches.

Nspecies

integer or NULL. Cap species to the top N (others merged to "other").

NspeciesQuantile

numeric in (0,1] or NULL. Choose the smallest N covering this fraction of individuals. Used only when Nspecies is NULL: if both are given, Nspecies takes precedence.

rates

"annual" (default) or "interval": the unit of growth and mort. "annual" returns them per year, for a model simulated in yearly steps: a tree's growth over an interval of \(p\) years is \((dbh/dbh_{before})^{1/p} - 1\), and the mortality of a cohort is \(1 - (1 - n_{died}/n_{at\,risk})^{1/p}\), the constant yearly rates that compound to what was observed over the interval. "interval" returns them over the whole interval (dbh/dbh_before - 1 and n_died / n_at_risk), the output of FINN 0.1.0, for a model in which one simulation step is one census interval. \(p\) is year - year_before in the units of year, so year must be the calendar year of the inventory.

Value

A list with:

  • obs_dt: observations at site or patch level, one row per site (and patch), inventory year and species. period_length is the number of years since the site's previous inventory (NA at its first). growth is the mean relative diameter growth rate of the surviving trees (per year, or over the interval, see rates), and growth_n is how many trees that mean rests on. Both matter: means are aggregated across patches TREE-WEIGHTED (by growth_n), because that is the quantity the model predicts - it simulates sum(g*trees)/sum(trees) over the whole site, so an unweighted mean of patch means would be a different number. growth_n also travels with the response so fit can weight the likelihood by it: 34% of patch-level growth observations rest on a single tree while others average 30+, and the variance of a mean is \(\sigma^2/n\). Mortality comes back as a closed-cohort pair of counts, n_at_risk (trees alive at the start of the interval) and n_died (how many of them were dead at the end), plus the derived rate mort (NA where no cohort was at risk): the yearly rate 1 - (1 - n_died / n_at_risk)^(1 / period_length), or n_died / n_at_risk with rates = "interval". fit() scores mort with the binomial loss weighted by n_at_risk. reg is the number of recruits per hectare over the interval.

  • tree_dt: input trees with added growth fields and species recode: year_before, dbh_before, period_length (years since the tree's previous record), rel_growth (the increment over the interval, dbh/dbh_before - 1) and growth (the tree's growth rate in the unit of rates, the quantity behind obs_dt$growth and the growth column of fit(tree_data = )); an input column growth is replaced.

Details

FINN simulates the forest in steps of one year. With rates = "annual" the observation table is in the units that fit() compares with such a simulation: fit() compounds the simulated yearly growth and mortality of the period_length years before each census into one rate per year with the same functional (the geometric mean of \(1 + g\) minus one, one minus the geometric mean survival), and sums the simulated recruits over them (see finn_data). rates = "interval" belongs with resolveSiteIDs(time_axis = "census"), where one simulation step is one census interval and nothing is compounded. The counts (n_at_risk, n_died, growth_n) and reg stay quantities of the whole interval in both modes: the counts weight the likelihood by the number of trees behind an observation, and reg is compared with the recruits summed over the interval. To use the table, express year as years since the first inventory, give env one row per site and year from 1 to the last census, and build the initial cohorts from the first inventory; resolveSiteIDs does all three.

See also

resolveSiteIDs for the next step (integer ids, the annual time axis, the initial cohorts), finn_data for the tables fit takes, fia_obs_dt for a finished example, and vignette("C-Data_preparation", package = "FINN")

Examples

library(data.table)
# A tree list of eight Oregon FIA plots with four patches and three inventories
# each, one row per tree and inventory: siteName, patchName, treeName, year,
# species_name, dbh (cm), status ("new", "alive", "dead") and living.
tree_dt <- fread(system.file("extdata", "example_tree_dt.csv", package = "FINN"))
head(tree_dt[, .(siteName, patchName, treeName, year, species_name, dbh, status)])
#>    siteName  patchName       treeName  year          species_name    dbh status
#>      <char>     <char>         <char> <int>                <char>  <num> <char>
#> 1: 11_66410 11_66410_1 11_66410_1_100  2001 Pseudotsuga menziesii 47.244    new
#> 2: 11_66410 11_66410_1 11_66410_1_100  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 57.404  alive
#> 3: 11_66410 11_66410_1 11_66410_1_100  2021 Pseudotsuga menziesii 65.024  alive
#> 4: 11_66410 11_66410_2 11_66410_2_103  2001 Pseudotsuga menziesii 26.924    new
#> 5: 11_66410 11_66410_2 11_66410_2_103  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 30.734  alive
#> 6: 11_66410 11_66410_2 11_66410_2_103  2021 Pseudotsuga menziesii 34.036  alive

obs <- makeObsData(
  tree_dt[complete == TRUE],    # fully remeasured plots only
  plotsize          = 0.06,     # ha per patch; recruits are scaled to per hectare
  aggregate_by_site = FALSE,    # keep the patches: resolveSiteIDs() needs them
  fix_period_length = 10,       # drop plots whose remeasurement interval is not 10 years
  NspeciesQuantile  = 0.98)     # species covering 98 % of the stems; the rest is "other"
#> excluded 0 sites due to period length not beeing 10
#> excluded 0 sites due to dbh_growth being not within the range of -10 and 50
#> Nspecies set to 11 to cover 98% of individuals
#> Selected species: Pseudotsuga menziesii, Pinus ponderosa, Tsuga mertensiana, Pinus contorta, Abies grandis, Pinus monticola, Abies concolor, Abies shastensis, other, Juniperus occidentalis, Larix occidentalis
#> Combined 4 unselected species into 'other'
#> actuall number of species including 'others' is 12
#> Filtered to sites with at least 2 years and all patches having the same number of years:
#> Sites with 3 Inventories: 1056
#> Sites have between 4 and 4 patches
#> Kept obs_dt unaggregated by siteName. For aggregated data, set aggregate_by_site = TRUE
head(obs$obs_dt)
#>    siteName  patchName  year   species_name    ba   dbh trees growth growth_n
#>      <char>     <char> <int>         <char> <num> <num> <int>  <num>    <int>
#> 1: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2001 Abies concolor     0    NA     0     NA        0
#> 2: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2011 Abies concolor     0    NA     0     NA        0
#> 3: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2021 Abies concolor     0    NA     0     NA        0
#> 4: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2001  Abies grandis     0    NA     0     NA        0
#> 5: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2011  Abies grandis     0    NA     0     NA        0
#> 6: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2021  Abies grandis     0    NA     0     NA        0
#>     mort n_at_risk n_died   reg period_length
#>    <num>     <int>  <int> <num>         <int>
#> 1:    NA         0      0     0            NA
#> 2:    NA         0      0     0            10
#> 3:    NA         0      0     0            10
#> 4:    NA         0      0     0            NA
#> 5:    NA         0      0     0            10
#> 6:    NA         0      0     0            10

# mortality is a closed cohort: the trees alive at the start of the interval
# and how many of them had died by its end; `mort` is the yearly rate over the
# period_length years of the interval
obs$obs_dt[n_at_risk > 0, .(siteName, patchName, year, period_length, species_name,
                            n_at_risk, n_died, mort)][1:5]
#>    siteName  patchName  year period_length          species_name n_at_risk
#>      <char>     <char> <int>         <int>                <char>     <int>
#> 1: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2011            10 Pseudotsuga menziesii         1
#> 2: 11_66410 11_66410_1  2021            10 Pseudotsuga menziesii         1
#> 3: 11_66410 11_66410_2  2011            10 Pseudotsuga menziesii         8
#> 4: 11_66410 11_66410_2  2021            10 Pseudotsuga menziesii         8
#> 5: 11_66410 11_66410_3  2011            10 Pseudotsuga menziesii         4
#>    n_died       mort
#>     <int>      <num>
#> 1:      0 0.00000000
#> 2:      0 0.00000000
#> 3:      0 0.00000000
#> 4:      1 0.01326438
#> 5:      0 0.00000000
# growth is a yearly rate too, and travels with the number of trees behind it
obs$obs_dt[growth_n > 0, .(siteName, year, species_name, growth, growth_n)][1:5]
#>    siteName  year          species_name      growth growth_n
#>      <char> <int>                <char>       <num>    <int>
#> 1: 11_66410  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.019669783        1
#> 2: 11_66410  2021 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.012542247        1
#> 3: 11_66410  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.011816466        8
#> 4: 11_66410  2021 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.007917063        7
#> 5: 11_66410  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.018626114        4

# the same table with the rates over the whole ten-year interval (FINN 0.1.0)
obs10 <- makeObsData(tree_dt[complete == TRUE], plotsize = 0.06, aggregate_by_site = FALSE,
                     fix_period_length = 10, NspeciesQuantile = 0.98, rates = "interval")
#> excluded 0 sites due to period length not beeing 10
#> excluded 0 sites due to dbh_growth being not within the range of -10 and 50
#> Nspecies set to 11 to cover 98% of individuals
#> Selected species: Pseudotsuga menziesii, Pinus ponderosa, Tsuga mertensiana, Pinus contorta, Abies grandis, Pinus monticola, Abies concolor, Abies shastensis, other, Juniperus occidentalis, Larix occidentalis
#> Combined 4 unselected species into 'other'
#> actuall number of species including 'others' is 12
#> Filtered to sites with at least 2 years and all patches having the same number of years:
#> Sites with 3 Inventories: 1056
#> Sites have between 4 and 4 patches
#> Kept obs_dt unaggregated by siteName. For aggregated data, set aggregate_by_site = TRUE
obs10$obs_dt[growth_n > 0, .(siteName, year, species_name, growth, growth_n)][1:5]
#>    siteName  year          species_name     growth growth_n
#>      <char> <int>                <char>      <num>    <int>
#> 1: 11_66410  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.21505376        1
#> 2: 11_66410  2021 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.13274336        1
#> 3: 11_66410  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.12644955        8
#> 4: 11_66410  2021 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.08319808        7
#> 5: 11_66410  2011 Pseudotsuga menziesii 0.20321636        4
